title: v1.3: ensemble-domain axes (N_SEEDS, N_TEMPERATURES, N_NOISES, N_REPLICAS)
description: Phase 2 (commit 704037f) added the FITTING-domain axes (N_ATOMS, N_BONDS, N_ANGLES, N_TORSIONS, N_CONFORMERS, N_MOLS) — sufficient for §7.1 paper-grade bonded fitting. tev_design has additional ensemble-domain axes for inference (N_SAMPLES, N_TEMPERATURES, N_NOISES, N_JACOBIAN_PAIRS, N_COMBINE, N_APC_PAIRS). Prolix MD analogs needed when ensemble methods land: N_SEEDS (replicate sweeps), N_TEMPERATURES (replica exchange / parallel tempering), N_NOISES (Langevin friction sensitivity), N_REPLICAS (replica-exchange independent of seeds). Wire as AxisSpec instances in src/prolix/tiling/axes.py with appropriate cardinalities and heterogeneous flags. Pair with BatchPlan dispatch coverage in FittingPlan (already wired via task #48; just need to extend dispatch to these new axes for any ensemble-aware FittingPlan variant). Cheap incremental work when v1.3 ensemble methods land. Not blocking §7.1.

Separately confirmed: .praxia/backlog.jsonl and .praxia/debt.jsonl are stale, disjoint local journals that do NOT reflect the live DB (concrete example: backlog.jsonl marked B1-SETTLE-STACK completed while live DB id 3515 still showed open) -- query via mcp__praxia__backlog/debt with status='open' and an absolute workspace path, not these jsonl files.

title: settle_langevin advances positions at 0.5*dt (half_dt passed into an already-halving A-step)
description: RUN-VERIFIED (task 260806_p5_measurement_pipeline_audit). _langevin_step_a (src/prolix/physics/settle.py:2069-2074) already multiplies by 0.5 internally, so callers must pass the FULL dt. settle_langevin passes half_dt at settle.py:1233 and :1288, so each A-step advances 0.25*dt*v and a full cycle advances 0.5*dt*v instead of BAOAB's dt*v. Nine other _langevin_step_a call sites in the same file (1430,1439,1456,1709,1720,1996,1997,2495,2496) pass _dt. Measured ratio EXACTLY 0.5000 via a free-particle test (gamma=0, zero force, uniform translation): tests/physics/test_transrot_decomposition.py::test_settle_langevin_advances_positions_by_full_dt (xfail strict). The invariant x(t+dt)=x(t)+dt*v for a force-free friction-free particle is convention-independent, so this is unambiguous. Momentum kicks (dt*F) and OU decay (exp(-gamma*dt)) are CORRECT -- only positions are affected, which is why every temperature-based assertion still passes. IMPACT: the dt=1.0 fs gate (job 15870804) propagated positions as though dt=0.5 fs and a nominal 50 ps run covered ~25 ps -- a direct competing explanation for why the cap lift succeeded. Survived because no test checks per-step displacement: the OpenMM parity test compares FORCES at fixed positions (rmse<3.0) and otherwise asserts only finite energies and mean T in a 150-520 K band; kUPS trajectory cross-validation was skipped (not installed). FIX: pass _dt at :1233 and :1288 and reconcile the constraint-impulse divisors at :1262 and :1313, which currently divide by half_dt consistently with the INTENDED semantics. Requires re-validation of all recorded NVT results. FIXED 2026-08-06 (user-authorised): settle.py:1233 and :1288 now pass _dt. The dp impulse divisors at :1263 and :1313 needed NO change -- they divide by half_dt, which is the true duration of the A(dt/2) sub-step once the A-step itself is correct, so fixing the argument made both consistent. tests/physics/test_transrot_decomposition.py::test_settle_langevin_advances_positions_by_full_dt now measures exactly 1.0000 and passes. STATUS: fix landed and unit-verified, but NOT yet validated at scale -- every temperature-control test in tests/physics/test_settle_temperature_control.py is marked slow and so has never run in the fast CI gate. The dt<=1.0 fs cap must be re-gated on the cluster (rerun p5_nvt_gate_dt1fs.py, previously job 15870804) before the cap-lift claim can be restated, since the original gate propagated positions at an effective 0.5 fs. VALIDATED 2026-08-07: re-gated at genuine dt=1.0 fs, job 19774893 (895 waters, T_rot=298.93+-0.29 K, holds). GPU disambiguation of an unrelated fast-suite failure (test_settle_preserves_water_geometry: CPU segfault jobs 19848713/19849325, GPU timeout job 19853575) confirmed via git diff that cfd2b85 touches the same settle_positions call path, but the timeout was resolved purely by jit-wrapping the test's un-jitted 1000-step eager loop (commit d5a7048) -- job 19875071 then passed cleanly on GPU with no other settle/BAOAB-path failures among the run's 7 failed/23 errors (all in unrelated subsystems: XTC streaming, HLO compile-sharing, fitting/train, GBSA+proxide parsing). No evidence the propagator fix caused either failure mode. Size sweep ba334c1f re-run at genuine dt=1.0 fs (2026-08-11, campaign 46a4d737, jobs 19882395/19898460/19898934): crossover conclusion unchanged (N*=16 +-15K, N*=64 +-5K, T_rot faithful at every size). CLOSED THE LAST GAP 2026-08-11: tests/physics/test_settle_temperature_control.py::test_dt_sweep_16water_nvt[dt1.0fs] -- the slow-marked test flagged above as never having run under the corrected propagator -- was run directly (uv run pytest -k 'test_dt_sweep_16water_nvt and dt1.0fs' -m "") and PASSED (T_rot within +-15K of 300K, n=16, gamma=10, 10ps, seed=777). The 'resolved' status is now backed by all three lines of evidence: unit test, cluster-scale gate, and the size-sweep re-validation.

title: settle_lfmiddle_langevin advances positions at 1.5*dt and applies half-strength friction
description: RUN-VERIFIED (task 260806_p5_measurement_pipeline_audit). settle_lfmiddle_langevin's apply_fn calls _langevin_step_a THREE times (settle.py:1430, :1439, :1456) while the comment at :1452-1454 states the intent is two ('A(0.5) second half -- mirrors first half for time-reversibility'). Since _langevin_step_a advances 0.5*dt*v, the cycle advances 1.5*dt*v instead of dt*v; measured ratio EXACTLY 1.5000 by the same free-particle test. CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (same task, on closer reading): an earlier version of this entry claimed the O-step applies half-strength friction. That is WRONG. There are TWO half_dt O-steps -- settle.py:1434/:1437 and :1466/:1469 -- which compose to exp(-gamma*dt/2)*exp(-gamma*dt/2) = exp(-gamma*dt). The friction is correct, and the split is the deliberate 'LFMiddle O-step splitting' described in CLAUDE.md. Only the extra A-step is a defect. NOT fixed alongside settle_langevin, because with a correctly-split O-step the question of WHICH of the three A-steps is spurious is a design decision about the intended LF-Middle scheme (the natural symmetric form puts the SETTLE velocity constraint between the two O halves, whereas the current code puts an A-step plus a force evaluation there), not a typo with one obvious correction. CONSEQUENCE: campaign 89c9a900 ('LFMiddle hypothesis FALSIFIED', 46 runs, 0 passes, mean T up to 3.35e57 K, documented in CLAUDE.md and v1.1_next_steps.md) tested THIS propagator. That campaign falsified a broken implementation, not the LF-Middle splitting -- the documented falsification does not support the conclusion drawn from it. Pinned by tests/physics/test_transrot_decomposition.py::test_lfmiddle_langevin_advances_positions_by_full_dt (xfail strict). Decide whether to fix and re-run, or to withdraw the falsification claim.

title: trans/rot decomposition divides un-COM-subtracted ke_trans by 3N-3 (8 hand-copied instances)
description: RUN-VERIFIED (task 260806_p5_measurement_pipeline_audit). Every copy computes ke_trans from per-water COM velocities WITHOUT subtracting the system COM velocity, then divides by dof_trans = 3N-3, a count valid only if the system COM has been removed. settle_langevin defaults remove_linear_com_momentum=False (settle.py:1022) and the Phase 5 scripts pass False explicitly. The COM is a live thermalized 3-DOF mode (settle.py:2120 draws each water's COM velocity independently from N(0,kT/M), so E[KE_com]=3kT/2 exactly) and, being force-free, its BAOAB O-step is exact, pinning its energy at the thermostat target. Bias is ADDITIVE: T_trans += 3*T_target/(3N-3) => +300 K at n=2, +20 K at n=16, +4.8 K at n=64, +0.34 K at n=895. Sampling the repo's own MB initializer with NO dynamics reproduces the documented table (603.8 K vs recorded 600.6 K at n=2; 319.6 K vs 319.67 K at n=16). Correcting the recorded per-seed JSONs flattens the documented '~1/N translational finite-size decay' to within 1.22 K of 300 K across a 450x size range; combined residual n>=64 is +0.39+-0.22 K (1.75 sigma, NS). T_rot is exactly Galilean-invariant under this estimator, so 'T_rot is faithful at every size' is a theorem about the metric, not evidence. The gate's decision variable IS T_rot (p5_nvt_gate_dt1fs.py:207), so the dt<=1.0 fs cap lift is not undermined by THIS defect (see debt_settle_langevin_half_dt_position_advance for one that may). AFFECTED (all 8 + 1 indirect): scripts/experiments/p5_nvt_gate_dt1fs.py:90-106, p5_nvt_gate_diag.py:90-106, p5_nve_transrot_bisect.py:125-135, p5_dt_scaling_transrot.py:113-119; scripts/explore/p5_transrot_decomp.py:57-65, p5_rot_substep.py:49-58, p5_r1_r2_reference_bias.py:92-100; tests/physics/test_settle_temperature_control.py:97,103-108; plus src/prolix/physics/rigid_water_ke.py:40-43 (same 6N-3-without-COM-removal error in the T_total path). FIX: extract ONE decompose_transrot() into src/prolix/physics/ that subtracts the system COM velocity and returns ke_com as a first-class observable -- valid regardless of the remove_linear_com_momentum setting -- and delete the copies. Also reconcile settle.py:1893 and :2325, where CSVR defaults remove_com=True but that flag only feeds _n_dof_thermostated (:2047-2051) with NO actual COM-removal operation: a CSVR targeting (6N-3)kT/2 on a system with a free COM is the textbook flying-ice-cube setup and a plausible mechanism for the documented NPT 1e115 K runaway.
